title: Forgiveness of Sins
definition: Forgiveness of Sins is God's gracious removal of guilt and condemnation through the blood of Jesus Christ.
summary: Forgiveness of Sins is God's gracious removal of guilt through the blood of Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ has authority to forgive sins and secures forgiveness through His death and resurrection.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Forgiveness of sins is God's gracious removal of guilt through the blood of Christ. Scripture does not treat sin as a small mistake but as real offense against God that must be dealt with by real mercy.

Forgiveness means God does not hold the believer's sins against them because Christ has borne them. The debt is not ignored; it is paid by the Savior.

Jesus is the One in whom forgiveness is proclaimed. His cross gives guilty people a clean conscience, and His resurrection assures them that the payment was accepted.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because guilt can either harden people in hiding or crush them in despair. Forgiveness answers both by bringing sinners into the light where sin is confessed and mercy is received through Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Confess sin honestly instead of excusing it or hiding it. Receive forgiveness through Christ with gratitude, and become a person who extends mercy because you know what it cost God to forgive you.
